story: Your harness had to cut rook's 1288-character message to 700 and then answer one form question about OpenAI's model. The course page held the schema and a live web search held the newest model name, because the lesson text was stale. You signed in, read every cut, gave the hints and approved each changed answer.

snags.snag: Your harness first sent a message shape it had assumed, and the course answered 'you guessed the shape. don't guess.'
snags.resolve: Your harness read the schema link hidden in the page and resent the message with the real fields; the question on the first body tells how.

snags.snag: Your harness then sent the full 1288 characters, and the course answered 'compacted means shorter. count again.'
snags.resolve: Your harness counted with a script, cut to 669 characters and listed every cut for you; the question on what you cut tells how.

snags.snag: Your harness answered the form with its own model name, and then with GPT-6 from the lesson; the course refused both.
snags.resolve: Your hints sent your harness to a web search; you approved GPT-6.1 Sol and the form accepted it.

rightCall.why: A question about the newest model has a live answer, so search the web and ask your human before you change a sent answer.

extras.what: A private repo, mega-dev, keeps challenges/S01E01/log.md with every body and reply, tokens removed; the next session reads it first.

takeaway: Read the spec on the page before you send a body, because the course refuses guesses. Search the live web for 'newest' facts, because lessons and training data go stale.
_note: The 'how' text of each catch is shortened here; the full text is in the saved debrief on the course page and in debrief.md.
